Often referred to as the "Hermit Kingdom," the totalitarian regime maintains a near-total blockade on the flow of information, making accurate reporting a monumental challenge. Among the handful of Western news organizations that have managed to breach this digital and physical wall, CNN has played a pivotal role in bringing rare, inside perspectives of North Korea to a global audience.

Western journalists are rarely granted visas, and those permitted entry are subjected to round-the-clock government minders, scripted itineraries, and pervasive surveillance. Furthermore, during periods of rapid diplomacy—such as the historic summits between Kim Jong Un and former U.S. President Donald Trump—CNN was on the front lines, translating complex geopolitical maneuvers for millions of viewers in real time.

By interviewing defectors who have escaped across the border, analyzing satellite data on food insecurity, and observing daily life on the streets of Pyongyang, reporters attempt to paint a more nuanced picture of the North Korean people, who live under strict state censorship and severe economic hardship.
